Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 The Goal 2 Content 3 Playing the Game 3.1 Start Construction 3.2 Recruit a Worker 3.3 Send a Worker to Work 3.4 Take Coins 4 End of the Game 4.1 Tie Breakers The Goal You must get the most victory points by using your workers to construct buildings. Content Cards There are 84 cards: 34 Building cards plus 8 machines 42 Workers cards Coins There are 40 coins: 15 Golden Coins (Value 5) 25 Silver Coins (Value 1) Note: You will earn 1 victory point for every 10 coins at the end of the game Playing the Game On your turn you get to play 3 actions. If you wish you can pay 5 coins per each additional action. The Actions Start Construction Recruit a Worker Send a Worker Take Coins Start Construction (Cost 1 action) You can choose one building from the 5 open Building cards. Immediately replace the card with the top card from the building deck. You may repeat this action as long as you have actions during your turn. (Remember that for every 5 coins you pay to the bank you can get 1 more action) Machines A machine is built as a building and is worth victory points but when you build a machine it is treated as a worker that does not require payment for its work. Recruit a Worker (Cost 1 action) You can choose one worker from the 5 open Worker cards. Immediately replace the card with the top card from the worker deck. You may repeat this action as long as you have actions during your turn. (Remember that for every 5 coins you pay to the bank you can get 1 more action) Send a Worker to Work (variable action cost) When you send a worker you must pay the number of coins in the upper right corner of the Worker card. Once you send a worker to work on a building it can not move until the building is complete. Action cost of sending a Worker In addition to paying the coin cost on the card, the action cost of sending a worker increases for each worker you send to that same building during your turn. First worker sent to the building this turn = 1 action (regardless of the amount of workers already working on the building) Second worker sent to that building = 2 more actions (for a total of 3) Third worker sent to that building = 3 more actions (for a total of 6) And so on... Finishing a Building (is not an action) For completing the building you need to add workers until all of the requirements for the building are met or exceeded. You will earn the amount of coins shown on the building card from the bank and the amount of victory points. Take Coins (variable action cost) You can take Coins from the bank: For 1 action you can take 1 Coin For 2 actions you can take 3 Coins For 3 actions you can take 6 Coins End of the Game When a player gets 17 victory points from building alone (not coins) the game will end after each player finish their turn for that round. The player with the most amount of victory points will win the game, this time adding 1 more victory point for every 10 coins to the victory point received from the buildings and machines. Tie Breakers If there is a tie where both players have the same number of victory points, then the winner is whoever has more VPs from buildings alone (including machines, but not coins). If there is still a tie, then the winner is whoever has more coins. If there is still a tie, the game is drawn. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Fairly simple engine building race game, not too long unless AP.  The Antiquity version is slightly better. + Nice tension between managing money and your time (you can buy extra actions for +5c) – Crucial move is to hire Master workers quickly to churn out  buildings.  First player to do this usually has a big advantage and will win. With a random market draw so this often is determined by the game. – Building requirements are a little hard to see

[Rating: 2.5/10] Gameplay is too simpel. There is only one path to victory and the decisions are obvious. It felt very flat and uninspiring to me.

[Rating: 3/10] After reading the rulebook, the game sounded great. I enjoy drafting - here there are both buildings and workers to be drafted, separately. I like gathering resources and all that stuff. Unfortunately the game has almost zero interaction. You're not looking what other players are drafting, which worker on the board might actually help them, so you can snatch it right before them. Even if this happens to you, I bet that the opponent didn't do it on purpose. It's more like a multiplayer solitaire optimization game. Whoever first reaches 17 points wins the game. Advantages: short game, nice graph

[Rating: 3/10] Pretty mediocre. It's fine, but very forgettable. I played this once with 4 people. I wouldn't want to play with that count again. It would be best with 2, [i]maybe[/i] 3.  It is certainly multiplayer solitaire, something I don't generally mind, but some might. This is what hurts the game in a 4 player match. There is nothing interesting to pay attention to between turns. You could really play this solo and barely anything would change. You can theoretically take something important that another player might need, but it probably isn't a good idea strategically, as it would be more productive 

[Rating: 3/10] A basic set-matching game without even the memory element of 'Go Fish'. It's a matter of looking at the cards that are available and seeing if you have enough money to pay for those that will allow you to complete your building. The limited challenge lies simply in choosing those that work best together and that give you the best bang for your buck.

[Rating: 3/10] The game is very simple. You draft workers and buildings, assign workers to buildings, once the buildings are done you earn money and VP and race to get to 17 VP. There are no significant decisions to be made as it is really an efficiency game and your turn is spent identifying the fastest most efficient way to satisfy the requirements of finishing a building by matching workers to them. Not a good game, not even for a filler.

[Rating: 3/10] The Builders is the same game as Splendor, only with even less theme and fiddlier rules: they both are unattractive to me but at least Splendor plays more smoothly.
